purpose: Improve the character with one understandable, recoverable correction at a time.
evidence_scope: These approaches summarize observed development results and useful safeguards. A local success is not proof of quality on another character; no preset supplies anatomy, approval or native authorization.

cycle.title: Make the visible target clear
cycle.instruction: Mark what looks wrong on the actual image. Keep the user's exact words, accepted appearance and features to preserve together.

cycle.title: Choose the construction that fits the problem
cycle.instruction: Use qualified spatial support for shape. For motion, build a coherent mechanism first. Diagnose uncertainty only when the answer changes the next edit.

cycle.title: Build one recoverable comparison
cycle.instruction: The modeling owner makes an isolated trial. Compare the approved baseline and trial at the same view and pose, including the whole character, joins and affected motion.

cycle.title: Keep only the supported gain
cycle.instruction: Correct misunderstandings visibly. Check actual native results, reopen consequential changes, and retain useful outcomes with their limits. Technical checks and target agreement do not approve appearance.

methods.title: Fit intended shape with spatial support
methods.basis: Early overlapped guide/depth/section fits improved likeness; anatomically consistent supported guides produced a later owner-recognized improvement. Scoped rest smoothing was also accepted.
methods.when: The intended static form is clear and useful registered guide/depth/section support exists.
methods.method: Register the useful guide to justified stationary anchors. Name supported and excluded surfaces; constrain the local edit with the same registration, depth and corresponding sections used in review. Preserve connected transitions and inspect the actual resulting surface, not only a smooth displacement field.
methods.limits: Guide endpoints do not establish coherent motion. A previous accepted smoothing result does not prove a new bump/strain repair. Rejected guide depth is not a fitting target.
methods.reference: Use accepted identity artwork and locally qualified registered support. Show useful appearance images separately from geometry authority.

methods.title: Build motion as a connected mechanism
methods.basis: A connected construction with shared timing replaced accumulated pose corrections and produced an owner-recognized improvement. Subsequent carried attachments and compact baked motion were verified in that development case.
methods.when: Motion folds, sinks, zips or disrupts a feature despite improved endpoint scores.
methods.method: Study how a suitable reference constructs the moving feature. Adapt its mechanism to the character's anatomy, moving band, landing and attached parts, using one shared timing. Fit a few meaningful parameters with qualified posed guides; change construction or correspondence when recurring failures persist.
methods.limits: Reference anatomy, hinge versus slide, lower-feature travel and shape count are character-specific. Independent per-phase fields and added correction layers are known failure patterns, not recommended motion construction.
methods.reference: Show measured construction references alongside current character identity and qualified pose support. A reference avatar teaches mechanics, not replacement proportions.

methods.title: Find what causes the visible defect
methods.status: Demonstrated diagnosis; repair still needs proof
methods.basis: Source-bound coverage and realization checks caught omitted controls and canceled edits. Matched geometry/normal/lighting checks later distinguished a sampled geometric surface problem from ordinary normal recalculation.
methods.when: A bump, band or gap may come from geometry, shading, correspondence, occlusion or an edit that never reached the displayed mesh.
methods.method: Trace the marked pixels to the actual displayed/evaluated surface. Reproduce the saved baseline, then change one diagnostic condition that distinguishes the suspected causes. Check local depth/sections and corresponding native topology where relevant. Use the answer to select the smallest justified construction change.
methods.limits: A dark band is not automatically a geometric ridge. Normal recalculation is not a universal cure. Material stretch is not simulated tissue stress, and a seam/return should not be flattened as interior roughness.
methods.reference: Use matched bare-surface and complete-feature captures, plus qualified local appearance cues. Keep supported, excluded and unknown guide portions visible.

experimental.title: Unqualified local guide transfer or a new fairing recipe
experimental.status: Promising only where evidence supports it
experimental.instruction: Show built alternatives, exact source support and affected motion. Do not turn a smooth reference patch or synthetic score into accepted geometry.

experimental.title: Recurring pose patches, metric-only retention and contour drift
experimental.instruction: Stop equivalent sweeps. Revisit the construction and the user's actual target. Keep failed trials as history rather than default recommendations.
